evidence.text: The plans of the heart belong to man, but the reply of the tongue is from the LORD.
All a man’s ways are pure in his own eyes, but his motives are weighed out by the LORD.
Commit your works to the LORD and your plans will be achieved.
The LORD has made everything for His purpose—even the wicked for the day of disaster.
Everyone who is proud in heart is detestable to the LORD; be assured that he will not go unpunished.
By loving devotion and faithfulness iniquity is atoned for, and by the fear of the LORD one turns aside from evil.
When a man’s ways please the LORD, He makes even the man’s enemies live at peace with him.
A man’s heart plans his course, but the LORD determines his steps.
Honest scales and balances are from the LORD; all the weights in the bag are His concern.
Whoever heeds instruction will find success, and blessed is he who trusts in the LORD.
The lot is cast into the lap, but its every decision is from the LORD.

c: Wealth and Poverty in the Wisdom Literature
The sayings in Scripture about wealth and poverty, particularly in the wisdom literature, are individual snapshots of a broad truth: God blesses the wise with wealth (
), while foolish behavior—especially laziness—leads to poverty (see
The book of Proverbs readily acknowledges that some wicked fools are wealthy, but it also reminds us that this kind of wealth will not last long (
). Poverty can sometimes result from injustice (
) rather than foolishness, and wealth sometimes comes from injustice and dishonesty (
). Those who have wealth need to use it wisely, which includes generosity to those in need (
The benefits of wealth are limited. Occasionally, wealth produces problems rather than solving them (
). Because wisdom can help where wealth cannot, wisdom is much more important than money (
All things being equal, the godly will be rewarded with material blessings and the opportunity to be generous. However, all things are not equal. Sometimes wealth does not go to the deserving (see
), nor does it necessarily produce satisfaction (see
). In fact, money can be detrimental to faith (
). When a choice must be made between godliness and money, the wise will choose godliness.
